stories.headline: OpenAI releases 722 math papers in 372 result families from an unreleased internal model

key_facts.fact: On October 6, 2026 OpenAI released a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model, saying it consulted the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI at the Institute for Advanced Study.
key_facts.excerpt: We're releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. We've been consulting with the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study

key_facts.fact: The release comprises 722 manuscripts grouped into 372 result families, published in a GitHub repository; the model was given about 4,000 problems.
key_facts.excerpt: The Sam Altman-led AI startup has released 722 manuscripts spanning 372 groups of results ... the internal frontier model was given about 4,000 mathematical problems

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the average result used compute equivalent to roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking, and it published 10 summaries of the model's reasoning.
key_facts.excerpt: These include 10 summaries of the model's reasoning, estimations of compute spent in terms of Pro usage on ChatGPT, and statistics about the number of attempted problems. The average result used the equivalent compute of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.

key_facts.fact: Claimed results include a solution to the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture and progress toward the Riemann hypothesis; many results are verified in the Lean proof language.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the results claimed are a solution to the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, improvements on some of the world's most important computer algorithms and actual progress toward math's scariest problem, the Riemann hypothesis.

key_facts.fact: An OpenAI spokesperson said the unreleased model produced almost every result from a single prompt to a single AI agent, unlike the 10,000-agent swarm used for its earlier Navier-Stokes claim.
key_facts.excerpt: produced almost every one of the results in response to a single prompt handed to a single AI agent. This would be a striking difference from OpenAI's earlier blockbuster solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, which was produced through the collective efforts of a 10,000-strong agentic swarm

key_facts.fact: OpenAI did not publish prompts or per-result compute as the advisory group recommended, saying it is not bound by the recommendations; it says it is working to release the model.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is choosing only to reveal the average compute time for a problem, with some additional statistics—and no prompts. The OpenAI spokesperson told Scientific American that the team is taking the advisory group's guidelines seriously ... but added that the company is not bound by these recommendations.

key_facts.fact: Family 003 claims no Dirichlet L-function, including the Riemann zeta function, has a zero with real part above 7/8 (a 'quasi-Riemann hypothesis'); the repository lists 162 papers with a formalized main result.
key_facts.excerpt: No Dirichlet L-function, the Riemann zeta function included, has a zero with real part above 7/8, which the entry calls the quasi-Riemann hypothesis ... the repository's catalogue lists 162 papers with a formalized main result.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman reacted to the release by writing 'We are entering a new era of discovery now.'
key_facts.excerpt: We are entering a new era of discovery now

stories.headline: Mistral previews Large 4 'Le Chonk', a 1T-parameter model with open weights due October 27

key_facts.fact: Mistral AI launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active, available via preview API on Mistral Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral AI has launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active parameters, available through a preview API on Mistral Studio.

key_facts.fact: ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own European datacenters.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European datacenters.

key_facts.fact: Mistral says weights will be released on October 27, after red-teaming with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners and state authorities; it calls it the most powerful open-weight system outside China.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral has released a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1T model that the Paris-based company says is the most powerful open-weight AI system outside China ... The model weights ... will be available on October 27.

key_facts.fact: Documentation lists 1.05 trillion total parameters, a one-million-token context window, and pricing of $0.68 per million input tokens and $2.09 per million output tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: 1.05 trillion total parameters, 49 billion active parameters, and a 1.6-billion-parameter vision encoder, alongside a one-million-token context window ... pricing of $0.68 per million input tokens, $0.07 per million cached input tokens, and $2.09 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Mistral says ML4 is competitive with the strongest open-source models globally while significantly outperforming any open-weight model developed in the US or Europe, and is state-of-the-art among open models on cybersecurity, finance and law.
key_facts.excerpt: It already achieves performance competitive with the strongest open-source models globally, while significantly outperforming any open-weight model developed in the US or Europe. On critical enterprise workloads, including cybersecurity, finance and law, we find it to be state-of-the-art among open models.

stories.headline: Anthropic merges Glasswing into a 3-tier cyber program opening Mythos 5.1 to vetted defenders

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched an expanded Cyber Verification Program with three access tiers, each including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1 and future models.
key_facts.excerpt: The program now consists of three access tiers ... Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward.

key_facts.fact: The revamp integrates the CVP and Project Glasswing, which previously gave organizations securing critical software access to Mythos, into a single offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic on Tuesday announced a revamped Cyber Verification Program (CVP), integrating the CVP and Project Glasswing into a single offering, with three levels of access to its most capable AI models.

key_facts.fact: Tiers are Defense Access, Red Team Access (adds authorized penetration testing) and Specialized Access for testing systems like power grids, flight systems and interbank transfer infrastructure, vetted with the US government.
key_facts.excerpt: Specialized Access has the fewest cybersecurity blocks and is reserved for a limited group of verified organizations authorized to test high-risk systems ... The company reviews each applicant in collaboration with the US government.

key_facts.fact: On the CyScenarioBench evaluation, Opus 5.5 was blocked on every task without CVP; in Red Team Access it completed 34 of 50 tasks, roughly its 67.6% unsafeguarded success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: Without CVP access, every task was blocked on the first prompt ... In the Red Team Access tier, no blocks occurred, and Claude Opus 5.5 successfully completed 34 of the 50 tasks—effectively equivalent to the model's 67.6% success rate on this evaluation with no safeguards applied

key_facts.fact: Program members must accept data retention so Anthropic can monitor misuse until 'Enterprise Frontier Safeguards' arrives later this fall.
key_facts.excerpt: Data retention is required for organizations enrolled in ... program so that we can monitor for cyber misuse. Once Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) ... is available later this fall, eligible organizations will be able to store data in cloud infrastructure they control.

key_facts.fact: The change comes a week after Anthropic warned about the cyber capabilities of Z.ai's open GLM-5.3 model.
key_facts.excerpt: Only a week after warning about the perils of competitor Z.ai's GLM-5.3 model and its advanced cybersecurity capabilities, Anthropic has expanded its Cyber Verification Program (CVP) – or rather, reconfigured it.

stories.headline: Musk says Grok Bot will route tasks to rival models including Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, Suno

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk posted that SpaceX will use 'the best back end model for any given task, including Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno and other leading APIs' for Grok Bot.
key_facts.excerpt: "Going forward, @SpaceX will use the best back end model for any given task, including Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno and other leading APIs. Whatever is most likely to give you the best outcome," Musk wrote.

key_facts.fact: The Information reported the announcement came Tuesday night and signals a shift by SpaceX's AI unit toward using competitors' models.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk announced on Tuesday night that SpaceX's AI unit will now use some AI models from competitors to power Grok Bot, signaling a shift away

key_facts.fact: Grok Bot, the agent app from SpaceXAI, launched in August; the change came a day after users reported problems reaching Grok.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok Bot is the AI agent app from SpaceXAI, the AI business Musk has folded into SpaceX. It launched in August ... The change came a day after users reported problems reaching Grok on its mobile and web services

key_facts.fact: A Grok Bot team member said all bots will be powered by Claude Opus 5.5 and can spawn cloud agents running Cursor's models.
key_facts.excerpt: Lauren (@poteto), who works on Grok Bot at SpaceXAI, says all bots will be powered by Claude Opus 5.5. They'll also be able to spawn cloud agents running any of Cursor's models.

key_facts.fact: Grok Bot reached 418,000 weekly users in the week ended September 14; SpaceX's Colossus 1 compute is already rented to Anthropic, making SpaceXAI both supplier and customer.
key_facts.excerpt: reached 418,000 weekly users in the week ended 14 September 2026, according to Bloomberg ... It also deepens ties with Anthropic, which in May 2026 signed a deal to use all of the compute at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data centre

key_facts.fact: Musk did not specify which tasks go to which provider, how users' data is shared, or pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk did not identify which tasks go to which provider or explain how the selection works ... It also does not describe pricing

stories.headline: Nous Research raises $90M at $1.5B valuation to take its open-source Hermes agent to enterprises

key_facts.fact: Nous Research raised $90 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to bring open-source AI assistants to business users.
key_facts.excerpt: Nous Research has raised $90 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to bring open-source artificial intelligence assistants to business users.

key_facts.fact: Its Hermes open-source agent has been downloaded more than 22 million times since February.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup's Hermes tool has been downloaded more than 22 million times since February

key_facts.fact: The Series B was led by Robot Ventures with participation from Nvidia, Microsoft M12, Samsung and USV, taking total funding to about $158 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Robot Ventures led the round, with participation from NVIDIA, Microsoft M12, Samsung, USV, and others, bringing the company's total funding to approximately $158 million.

key_facts.fact: Nous reported about $36 million in annualized revenue as of mid-September and expects to exceed $100 million by year-end; Hermes stays free under the MIT license.
key_facts.excerpt: By mid-September, Nous reported an annualized revenue of approximately $36 million and expects to exceed $100 million before the end of the year ... Hermes remains free and open-source under the MIT license

key_facts.fact: Nous plans an enterprise version of Hermes, betting companies want open-source architecture with more control over their data.
key_facts.excerpt: The company plans to launch an open-source AI assistant tool aimed at enterprise users. It builds on Hermes, a local and cloud-based AI agent that handles search, coding, and image understanding.

stories.headline: Meta and Sierra launch Personal Agent Protocol with Walmart, Shopify, Stripe for agent-business links

key_facts.fact: Sierra's Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor announced Personal Agent Protocol, an open standard Meta and Sierra are developing with Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart.
key_facts.excerpt: Personal Agent Protocol — an open standard Meta and Sierra are developing along with industry partners at Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart that defines how personal agents interact with businesses.

key_facts.fact: The protocol is designed to handle authentication and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs or company agents.
key_facts.excerpt: We're designing it to handle authentication, empower consumers and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs or company agents. It's open for anyone to implement.

key_facts.fact: It is built on OAuth with guest, read-only and write access tiers; a v0.1 spec and reference implementation are planned for later in October, with payments a future extension.
key_facts.excerpt: 3 access tiers: guest session, user-granted read-only, user-granted write ... v0.1 spec, design workshops and a reference implementation planned for October 2026; payments, finer permissions and push notifications are future extensions

key_facts.fact: Stripe and Shopify are also members of Visa's rival Trusted Agent Protocol.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe and Shopify are among the partners. Both have already joined a rival protocol run by Visa.

key_facts.fact: The effort is meant to let agents like Meta's Muse, launched a month earlier, work with businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: Personal Agent Protocol is designed to enable agents like Meta's Muse work with businesses to get things done.

stories.headline: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT for Teens an 'unacceptable risk'; OpenAI disputes the tests

key_facts.fact: Common Sense Media said OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens, introduced in August, is an 'unacceptable risk' whose protections 'fall short of what the company promised.'
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT for Teens, introduced in August, has guardrails for teens ... Common Sense Media says that the teen protections offered by the feature "fall short of what the company promised."

key_facts.fact: The assessment found ChatGPT doesn't send parent alerts when it should, doesn't offer the right help in crises, and still does kids' homework.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT "doesn't send alerts to parents when it should," doesn't offer "the right help in crisis situations," and "still does kids' homework"

key_facts.fact: Tom Siegel of Common Sense's Youth AI Safety Institute said a teen can talk about self-harm for an hour without a parent alert and that ChatGPT should be adults-only until fixed.
key_facts.excerpt: "A teen can spend an hour talking about self-harm without their parent getting a single alert. Until OpenAI fixes that and proves it with independent testing, ChatGPT should be for adults only."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the testing may have begun and ended before parental controls had finished activating, making findings inaccurate; Common Sense said it stands by its methodology.
key_facts.excerpt: Our review of Common Sense Media's methodology shows that the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete ... We stand behind our testing methodology and our results.

sources.title: ChatGPT for Teens is an 'unacceptable risk,' says Common Sense Media
